question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 6 & -6 & 7\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & a & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & b & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the value of $\frac{a}{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that $D={P}^{-1}AP$ is a diagonalization of the matrix $A.$

From the diagonal matrix $D,$ we find that the eigenvalues of $A$ are

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=1\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=3.$

The second column of $P$ corresponds to $\lambda =1.$ Computing $A-\lambda I,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-1I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 6 & -6 & 7\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 \\ 6 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & -6 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. From the first equation we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}={x}_{2}-{x}_{3}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Comparing this with the second column of $P,$ we deduce that ${x}_{2}=0.$ Now, setting ${x}_{3}=-1$ and substituting our values for ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ into the general solution, we obtain the following: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=-\frac{1}{1}=-1.$
